nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cell as the unit of life
nodes.outcome: State that every living thing is made of cells and that each cell must be kept alive individually

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why life processes are needed
nodes.outcome: Explain that maintenance of a living body needs energy and material even when the body is at rest

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why diffusion is not enough
nodes.outcome: Explain why diffusion alone cannot supply a multicellular body, and that a transport system is therefore required

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Read a chemical equation
nodes.outcome: Identify reactants and products on either side of a chemical equation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Balance a chemical equation
nodes.outcome: Balance a simple chemical equation by adjusting coefficients only

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Autotroph vs heterotroph
nodes.outcome: Classify an organism as autotrophic or heterotrophic from how it obtains food

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Inputs of photosynthesis
nodes.outcome: Name carbon dioxide, water and sunlight as the inputs of photosynthesis

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Outputs of photosynthesis
nodes.outcome: Name glucose and oxygen as the outputs of photosynthesis

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Which side oxygen appears on
nodes.outcome: Identify that oxygen appears on the product side of the photosynthesis equation, not the reactant side

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Write the photosynthesis equation
nodes.outcome: Write the balanced equation for photosynthesis including the sunlight and chlorophyll condition

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of chlorophyll
nodes.outcome: State that chlorophyll absorbs light energy and is not itself consumed in the reaction

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Function of stomata
nodes.outcome: Explain that stomata are the pores through which gases enter and leave a leaf

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Guard cells open and close stomata
nodes.outcome: Explain that guard cells swell to open a stoma and shrink to close it, controlling water loss

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Order of the human digestive tract
nodes.outcome: Put mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine and large intestine in the order food passes through them

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Saliva breaks down starch
nodes.outcome: State that salivary amylase begins the breakdown of starch in the mouth

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why the stomach is acidic
nodes.outcome: Explain that hydrochloric acid creates the acidic medium pepsin needs and kills ingested microbes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Where absorption happens
nodes.outcome: Identify the small intestine as the site where digested food is absorbed into the blood

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why villi matter
nodes.outcome: Explain that villi increase surface area, and relate greater surface area to faster absorption

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Respiration is not breathing
nodes.outcome: Distinguish breathing, which moves air, from respiration, which releases energy inside cells

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: The respiration equation
nodes.outcome: Write the equation for aerobic respiration and recognise it as the reverse of photosynthesis

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Aerobic vs anaerobic
nodes.outcome: State whether oxygen is used, and compare the energy released, for aerobic and anaerobic respiration

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Lactic acid in muscles
nodes.outcome: Explain that muscles short of oxygen produce lactic acid, and connect this to cramp after exercise

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Anaerobic respiration in yeast
nodes.outcome: State that yeast produces alcohol and carbon dioxide anaerobically, and link this to dough rising

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of mitochondria
nodes.outcome: Identify the mitochondrion as the site of aerobic respiration in the cell

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: The heart is a pump
nodes.outcome: Describe the heart as a muscular pump that moves blood, not as a store of blood

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Name the four chambers
nodes.outcome: Name the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium and left ventricle

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Atria receive, ventricles pump
nodes.outcome: State that atria receive blood into the heart and ventricles pump blood out of it

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: The pulmonary circuit
nodes.outcome: Trace blood from the right ventricle to the lungs and back to the left atrium

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: The systemic circuit
nodes.outcome: Trace blood from the left ventricle to the body and back to the right atrium

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Double circulation
nodes.outcome: Explain that blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit, and say why

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why the left ventricle wall is thicker
nodes.outcome: Explain the thicker left ventricle wall by the higher pressure needed to reach the whole body

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Valves prevent backflow
nodes.outcome: Explain that heart valves make blood flow in one direction only

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: The four components of blood
nodes.outcome: Name plasma, red cells, white cells and platelets, and give each one job

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Haemoglobin carries oxygen
nodes.outcome: State that haemoglobin in red cells binds oxygen, and that its iron is why blood is red

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Platelets clot blood
nodes.outcome: Explain that platelets seal a wound by forming a clot

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Arteries go away, veins return
nodes.outcome: State that arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry it back, regardless of oxygen content

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why artery walls are thick
nodes.outcome: Relate thick elastic artery walls to the high pressure of blood leaving the heart

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why veins have valves
nodes.outcome: Explain that valves in veins stop low-pressure blood from flowing backwards

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Exchange happens in capillaries
nodes.outcome: Explain that capillary walls are one cell thick so materials can pass between blood and cells

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Why waste must be removed
nodes.outcome: Explain that cellular reactions leave toxic wastes such as urea that must be removed

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Kidneys filter the blood
nodes.outcome: State that the kidneys filter wastes out of blood and that urine leaves through the bladder

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: The nephron is the filtering unit
nodes.outcome: Identify the nephron as the microscopic unit that does the actual filtering in a kidney

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Selective reabsorption
nodes.outcome: Explain that glucose, salts and most water are reabsorbed into the blood while urea passes on

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: What dialysis does
nodes.outcome: Explain that a dialysis machine filters blood outside the body when the kidneys fail
